new.title: Wander the lake island village of Gölyazı
new.desc: Gölyazı is a village on a peninsula in Lake Uluabat, built on ancient Apollonia, with Greek-era churches, stone houses and a lakeside square. The surrounding Ramsar wetland is full of water lilies and fishing boats.
new.tip: Come near sunset and climb the theatre hill for the view. Weekdays are quieter.
new.q: Gölyazı Meydanı, Gölyazı Mahallesi, Nilüfer, Bursa

new.title: Take a boat tour round Lake Uluabat
new.desc: Local boats cross Lake Uluabat past reed beds and Halilbey Island. The lake is a Ramsar wetland known for water lilies and migratory birds.
new.tip: Boats leave from the Gölyazı quay; settle the price before boarding.
new.q: Gölyazı İskelesi, Gölyazı, Nilüfer, Bursa

new.title: Watch storks nest in Eskikaraağaç
new.desc: Eskikaraağaç, next to Gölyazı, is known as the Stork Village, and storks nest on its rooftops and poles each spring and summer. Stork festivals are held here.
new.tip: Visit March to August; early morning gives the best light.
new.q: Eskikaraağaç Köyü, Nilüfer, Bursa

new.title: Eat fried turna fish at Gönül Sofrası in Gölyazı
new.desc: A family-run lakeside restaurant in Gölyazı where reviewers recommend the fried turna (lake pike-perch) and a village breakfast. Fish are caught on the lake and sold at the village square.
new.tip: Ask what was caught that day.
new.q: Gölyazı Gönül Sofrası Et Balık Kahvaltı, Gölyazı Mahallesi, Nilüfer, Bursa

new.title: Visit the Mudanya Armistice House
new.desc: The stone house on the Mudanya waterfront where the armistice of 11 October 1922 was signed, ending the Turkish War of Independence. It has been a museum since 1937 and keeps the marble table İsmet İnönü is said to have broken.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; check opening hours before going.
new.q: Mudanya Mütareke Evi Müzesi, 12 Eylül Caddesi, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Stroll Mudanya's old streets and Ottoman mansions
new.desc: Mudanya's old quarter keeps 19th-century wooden and stone houses, among them the Tahir Paşa Mansion, around Girit Sokağı near the harbour.
new.tip: Walk it in the morning, then eat fish on the front.
new.q: Girit Sokağı, Mudanya Merkez, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Order fish soup and sea bass at Ablanın Yeri
new.desc: A popular Mudanya fish restaurant, recommended by reviewers for fish soup, calamari and grilled sea bass.
new.tip: Check the bill before paying, as some reviews advise.
new.q: Ablanın Yeri, Mudanya Sahil, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Grill the catch at Erol Balık facing Mudanya harbour
new.desc: A fish restaurant opposite the Mudanya harbour, praised for fresh grilled fish and sea views.
new.tip: Ask for a window table at sunset in summer.
new.q: Erol Balık Restaurant, Mudanya Limanı, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Grab a balık ekmek at Ercan Usta
new.desc: A casual fish-sandwich stand on Mudanya's front, with generous portions and a sea view.
new.tip: Cheap and quick; go before the evening rush.
new.q: Mudanya Eminönü Balık Ekmek Ercan Usta, Mudanya Sahil, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Wander the old Greek village of Tirilye
new.desc: Tirilye, called Zeytinbağı from the 1960s until 2012, is an old Greek town with Ottoman-era houses, olive groves and Byzantine churches. The Fatih Mosque began as a Byzantine church of St Stephen.
new.tip: Go on a weekday in the olive season, autumn.
new.q: Fatih Camii, Tirilye Mahallesi, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Taste olives and olive oil in Tirilye
new.desc: Olives and olive oil have been Tirilye's main livelihood for centuries, and local shops sell the harvest and let you sample it.
new.tip: The harvest runs about November to January.
new.q: Tirilye Çarşı, Tirilye Mahallesi, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Eat seafood by the harbour at Tirilye Balık
new.desc: A fish restaurant by Tirilye's harbour; the village menus lean on olive-oil dishes alongside fish.
new.tip: Some places nearby take cash only; ask first.
new.q: Tirilye Balık Otel, Eski Pazar Caddesi No:76, Tirilye Mahallesi, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Swim and eat fish along the Güzelyalı coast
new.desc: A quieter shore near Mudanya with coves and local swimming spots; the seafood restaurants there are known for fish soup and tahini halva.
new.tip: Swim June to September.
new.q: Güzelyalı Sahili, Güzelyalı Mahallesi, Mudanya, Bursa

new.title: Sample Gemlik olives at the town market
new.desc: Gemlik is Turkey's best-known olive town; its central market sells fresh olives, oil and fish. The International Gemlik Olive Festival is held in the last week of August.
new.tip: Festival week is busiest; autumn is harvest time.
new.q: Gemlik Çarşı, Cumhuriyet Mahallesi, Gemlik, Bursa

new.title: Visit Bursa's oldest olive tree in Göllüce
new.desc: Göllüce village in Orhangazi is home to Bursa's oldest olive tree, and visitors can taste olives there or join the harvest in November or December.
new.tip: Best in the harvest months.
new.q: Göllüce Mahallesi, İznik, Bursa

new.title: See Hagia Sophia in İznik, the Orhan Mosque
new.desc: İznik's Byzantine Hagia Sophia was converted into the Orhan Mosque after the Ottoman capture of 1331. It stands at the town's central crossroads next to the clock tower.
new.tip: Dress modestly; it is a working mosque again.
new.q: İznik Ayasofya Camii, İznik, Bursa

new.title: Walk İznik's Roman-Byzantine walls to the Lefke Gate
new.desc: İznik's walls run about 3 km with four main gates. The Lefke Gate in the east carries a Greek inscription dated AD 123, and the stretch towards the Yenişehir Gate is the best preserved at 10 to 13 m.
new.tip: Walk the Lefke to Yenişehir stretch in the afternoon light.
new.q: Lefke Kapı, İznik, Bursa

new.title: See İznik tiles at the Nilüfer Hatun Imaret museum
new.desc: Murat I built the imaret in 1388 for his mother Nilüfer Hatun. It is now the İznik Museum of Turkish-Islamic Arts, with finds from the İznik tile kilns.
new.tip: Check it is open; it has been closed for restoration before.
new.q: İznik Müzesi, Müze Sokak, Eşrefzade Mahallesi, İznik, Bursa

new.title: Admire the tiled minaret of İznik's Green Mosque
new.desc: Built between 1378 and 1387 in the reign of Murat I, the mosque has a minaret faced in glazed tiles about 25 m tall, a landmark of early Ottoman architecture.
new.tip: Avoid prayer times when visiting.
new.q: Yeşil Cami, Yeşilcami Mahallesi, İznik, Bursa

new.title: Find the Roman theatre and the Ottoman tile kilns
new.desc: The Roman theatre lies between the lake shore and the Yenişehir Gate. Excavations there unearthed a 14th to 15th-century tile workshop with 10 kilns.
new.tip: Reached down Tiyatro Sokak; wear sturdy shoes.
new.q: İznik Roma Tiyatrosu, Tiyatro Sokak, İznik, Bursa

new.title: See the sunken basilica in Lake İznik
new.desc: A Roman-style basilica from about AD 390 lies about 20 m offshore at 1.5 to 3 m depth. It was spotted from the air in 2014 and has been excavated since 2015; an underwater museum is planned.
new.tip: Best seen from the shore on calm days.
new.q: İznik Gölü Bazilika Sualtı Kalıntısı, Sahil, İznik, Bursa

new.title: Watch İznik tile masters at their workshops
new.desc: İznik tile making dates to the 15th century, and small ateliers cluster in the lanes near the Green Mosque and the museum.
new.tip: Ask to see the hand-painting.
new.q: İznik Çini Atölyeleri, Yeşilcami Mahallesi, İznik, Bursa

new.title: Stroll the İznik lakeshore promenade at sunset
new.desc: The promenade by the Lake Gate on the town's waterfront looks over Lake İznik; the western shore is best at sunset.
new.tip: Cafés sit along the promenade.
new.q: İznik Gölü Sahili, Göl Kapı, Kılıçaslan Mahallesi, İznik, Bursa

new.title: Eat plump köfte at Köfteci Yusuf in İznik
new.desc: A local chain known for juicy köfte, with its own ayran brand and an on-site butcher.
new.tip: Add kuzu şiş to the köfte.
new.q: Köfteci Yusuf, Atatürk Caddesi, İznik, Bursa

new.title: Taste the original İnegöl köfte at Besler
new.desc: İnegöl köfte is credited to Mustafa Efendi, who settled in İnegöl in the 1890s. The family-run Besler chain keeps the recipe of beef, lamb, onion and salt, rested a day.
new.tip: Order it with piyaz and ayran.
new.q: Besler İnegöl Köftecisi, İnegöl, Bursa

new.title: Order the köfte at Kasap Ali İnegöl Köfte
new.desc: A well-known butcher-run köfte house in İnegöl praised for traditional meatballs.
new.tip: Go at lunch; weekends are busy.
new.q: Kasap Ali İnegöl Köfte, İnegöl, Bursa

new.title: Eat köfte with homemade yoghurt at Buhara
new.desc: Buhara İnegöl Köftecisi is cited for its köfte, homemade yoghurt and ayran.
new.tip: Ask for extra yoghurt.
new.q: Buhara İnegöl Köftecisi, İnegöl, Bursa

new.title: Soak in the Oylat thermal springs
new.desc: Oylat in Saadet neighbourhood has been used as a spa for about 2,000 years; the main hamam spring is about 40 degrees C.
new.tip: Spa hotels sell day entry; ask first.
new.q: Oylat Kaplıcaları, Saadet Mahallesi, İnegöl, Bursa

new.title: Tour the Oylat Cave
new.desc: A 730 m show cave in Hilmiye village at the mouth of the Oylat canyon. Discovered in 2004 and opened in 2006, it has stalactites, stalagmites and cave pearls.
new.tip: It is cool inside; bring a jacket.
new.q: Oylat Mağarası, Hilmiye Mahallesi, İnegöl, Bursa

new.title: Walk to the Suuçtu waterfall
new.desc: The 36 to 38 m Suuçtu waterfall in Mustafakemalpaşa formed along a fault line and sits in a nature park with picnic areas and paths.
new.tip: Best in spring and autumn.
new.q: Suuçtu Şelalesi Tabiat Parkı, Mustafakemalpaşa, Bursa

new.title: Try kemalpaşa tatlısı at Dardağan Tatlı
new.desc: Kemalpaşa tatlısı is a syrupy cheese dessert from Mustafakemalpaşa with a geographical indication. Dardağan serves it plain, with milk or with cream.
new.tip: Try it with kaymak.
new.q: Dardağan Tatlı Meydan Şube, Mustafakemalpaşa Merkez, Mustafakemalpaşa, Bursa

new.title: Compare a second kemalpaşa tatlısı at Kemtat
new.desc: Kemtat Kemalpaşa Tatlıcısı on Balıkesir Caddesi is another dedicated shop for the town's cheese dessert.
new.tip: Buy a box to take away.
new.q: Kemtat Kemalpaşa Tatlıcısı, Tatkavaklı Mahallesi, Balıkesir Caddesi No:75, Mustafakemalpaşa, Bursa

new.title: See the Karacabey Stud Farm
new.desc: One of Turkey's oldest state horse-breeding farms, historically supplying horses for the Ottoman army, and still active.
new.tip: Ask before entering; some parts are not open to visitors.
new.q: Karacabey Tarım İşletmesi, Karacabey, Bursa

new.title: Visit the 1457 Karacabey Imaret Mosque
new.desc: The Karacabey (İmaret) Mosque was built by Karaca Bey in 1457 and is the town's main historic monument.
new.tip: Combine with the nearby Ulu Mosque.
new.q: Karacabey İmaret Camii, Karacabey, Bursa

new.title: Eat by the stream in Misi village
new.desc: Misi, also called Gümüştepe, has Bursa's ethnography museum, a silk house and streamside cafés.
new.tip: Go for a weekend lunch.
new.q: Misi Köyü, Gümüştepe Mahallesi, Nilüfer, Bursa

new.title: Ski the Uludağ Hotels Zone
new.desc: Uludağ's ski resort sits at about 1,865 m near the 2,543 m summit, with the hotel zone served by the cable car.
new.tip: Skis are not allowed in the cabins; rent on the mountain.
new.q: Uludağ Oteller Bölgesi, Uludağ, Osmangazi, Bursa

new.title: Hike to the Uludağ summit at Kartaltepe
new.desc: Kartaltepe, the highest point of Uludağ, is 2,543 m. Summer routes lead up from the Hotels Zone.
new.tip: Weather turns quickly; carry layers.
new.q: Kartaltepe, Uludağ Milli Parkı, Osmangazi, Bursa

new.title: Picnic and walk the forest at Sarıalan
new.desc: Sarıalan, at about 1,634 m in Uludağ National Park, is reached by cable car and has forest paths and picnic areas.
new.tip: Ride the cable car; check its hours.
new.q: Sarıalan, Uludağ Milli Parkı, Bursa

new.title: Eat grilled meat at a garden restaurant on the Sarıalan road
new.desc: Garden restaurants and steakhouses line the mountain road from the İnkaya plane tree to Sarıalan in Uludağ National Park.
new.tip: Pick a garden table; weekends fill up.
new.q: İnkaya Tarihi Çınar, Sarıalan Yolu, Osmangazi, Bursa

new.title: See Atatürk's wooden mansion in Yalova Termal
new.desc: The wooden mansion in Termal, where Atatürk stayed in the 1930s, is known as the Walking Mansion (Yürüyen Köşk) and now works as a small museum.
new.tip: Combine with the spa baths.
new.q: Termal Atatürk Köşkü, Termal, Yalova

new.title: Walk the Karaca Arboretum
new.desc: The Karaca Arboretum, founded by Hayrettin Karaca on about 13.5 hectares, holds thousands of plant species.
new.tip: Spring and autumn are best.
new.q: Karaca Arboretum, Yalova

new.title: Hike to the Sudüşen waterfall
new.desc: A forest trail in the Termal district leads to Sudüşen, the best-known of Yalova's waterfalls.
new.tip: Wear grip shoes; the trail can be wet.
new.q: Sudüşen Şelalesi, Termal, Yalova

new.title: Visit the twin Erikli waterfalls
new.desc: The double-tiered Erikli waterfall, about 15 m high, sits in forest with a camping area and village eateries.
new.tip: Best April to June.
new.q: Erikli Şelalesi, Teşvikiye, Çınarcık, Yalova

new.title: Dine at Başköşe in Termal
new.desc: The top-rated restaurant of Termal on TripAdvisor, in the spa district.
new.tip: Reserve at weekends.
new.q: Başköşe, Termal, Yalova

new.title: Eat at Doktorun Evi in Termal
new.desc: A well-reviewed restaurant in the Termal district near the spas.
new.tip: Check opening hours first.
new.q: Doktor'un Evi Restaurant, Üvezpınar, Termal, Yalova

new.title: Eat fish aboard Kıyı Balık Gemi
new.desc: A fish restaurant on a ship at the old ferry terminal on Yalova's waterfront.
new.tip: Sit on deck for sunset.
new.q: Kıyı Balık Gemi Restaurant, 15 Temmuz Demokrasi ve Cumhuriyet Meydanı, Rüstem Paşa Mahallesi, Yalova Merkez, Yalova

new.title: Order the day's catch at Kavancha Balık
new.desc: A Yalova city-centre fish restaurant in the same seafood cluster as Kıyı Balık.
new.tip: Ask for the catch of the day.
new.q: Kavancha Balık, Setur Marina Yat Limanı, Cengiz Koçal Caddesi, Süleymanbey Mahallesi, Yalova Merkez, Yalova

new.title: Swim in the Çınarcık bay
new.desc: The coast between Çınarcık and Armutlu has bays and swimming beaches on the Marmara.
new.tip: Swim June to September.
new.q: Çınarcık Plajı, Çınarcık, Yalova

new.title: Explore Sadağı Canyon in Orhaneli
new.desc: Sadağı Canyon Nature Park mixes canyon scenery, thermal springs and history in the Orhaneli district.
new.tip: Combine with the Aslanlı thermal baths.
new.q: Sadağı Kanyonu Tabiat Parkı, Sadağı Köyü, Orhaneli, Bursa

new.title: Raft the Kocasu River at Orhaneli
new.desc: The Kocasu River course in Orhaneli has 12 rapids along 8 km, the only rafting course in this part of the Marmara region.
new.tip: Spring has the best flow.
new.q: Orhaneli Rafting Parkuru, Kocasu Deresi, Orhaneli, Bursa
